verses.text: Meanwhile, Saul was still making threats to kill the Lord's followers. He went to the high priest
and asked him for letters to the synagogues in Damascus. He wanted to find any people who belonged to the Way, men or women, tie them up, and bring them back to Jerusalem.
As Saul came near Damascus on his journey, a light from heaven suddenly flashed around him.
He fell to the ground and heard a voice say to him, "Saul, Saul, why are you attacking me?"
Saul asked, "Who are you, Lord?" He answered, "I am Jesus, the one you are attacking.
Now get up and go into the city. There you will be told what you must do."
The men travelling with Saul stood there unable to speak. They heard the sound, but they did not see anyone.
Saul got up from the ground, but when he opened his eyes, he could not see anything. So they led him by the hand into Damascus.
For three days he was blind, and he did not eat or drink anything.
In Damascus there was a follower named Ananias. The Lord spoke to him in a vision: "Ananias!" He answered, "Yes, Lord, here I am."
The Lord told him, "Get up and go to the house of Judas on Straight Street. Ask for a man from Tarsus named Saul. He is praying right now.
In a vision he has seen a man named Ananias come in and place his hands on him so that he can see again."
Ananias answered, "Lord, I have heard many reports about this man and all the harm he has done to your people in Jerusalem.
And he has come here with authority from the chief priests to arrest all who call on your name."
But the Lord said to him, "Go! I have chosen this man to carry my name to the Gentiles and their kings, and to the people of Israel.
I will show him how much he must suffer for my name."

So Ananias went to the house and placed his hands on Saul. He said, "Brother Saul, the Lord Jesus, who appeared to you on the road as you were coming here, has sent me so that you may see again and be filled with the Holy Spirit."
At once something like scales fell from Saul's eyes, and he could see again. He got up and was baptised.
Then he ate some food and got his strength back. Saul spent several days with the followers in Damascus.
Right away he began to preach in the synagogues that Jesus is the Son of God.

All who heard him were amazed. They asked, "Is this not the man who caused so much harm in Jerusalem to those who call on this name? Did he not come here to arrest them and take them to the chief priests?"
But Saul grew more and more powerful. He confused the Jews living in Damascus by proving that Jesus is the Christ.
After many days had gone by, the Jews made a plan to kill Saul.
But Saul learned about their plan. Day and night they watched the city gates closely so that they could kill him.
But his followers took him one night and lowered him in a basket through an opening in the city wall.
When Saul came to Jerusalem, he tried to join the followers, but they were all afraid of him. They did not believe he was really a follower.

But Barnabas took him and brought him to the apostles. He told them how Saul had seen the Lord on the road and how the Lord had spoken to him. He also told them how boldly Saul had preached in the name of Jesus in Damascus.
So Saul stayed with them and went freely all around Jerusalem,
speaking boldly in the name of the Lord Jesus. He talked and argued with the Greek-speaking Jews, but they tried to kill him.
When the believers learned of this, they took him down to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus.

Then the church all through Judea, Galilee, and Samaria had a time of peace and grew strong. It kept growing in number as the believers lived in the fear of the Lord and were comforted by the Holy Spirit.
As Peter travelled around the country, he went to visit God's people who lived in Lydda.
There he found a man named Aeneas, who could not move and had been lying in bed for eight years.
Peter said to him, "Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you. Get up and make your bed." At once Aeneas got up.
Everyone who lived in Lydda and Sharon saw him, and they turned to the Lord.
In Joppa there was a follower named Tabitha. In Greek her name is Dorcas. She was always doing good and helping the poor.
About that time she became sick and died. Her body was washed and placed in an upstairs room.
Lydda was near Joppa. So when the followers heard that Peter was in Lydda, they sent two men to him. They begged him, "Please come at once!"

Peter got up and went with them. When he arrived, he was taken upstairs. All the widows stood around him, crying. They showed him the coats and other clothes Dorcas had made while she was still with them.
Peter sent them all out of the room. Then he got down on his knees and prayed. He turned towards the dead woman and said, "Tabitha, get up." She opened her eyes, and when she saw Peter, she sat up.
He took her by the hand and helped her to her feet. Then he called the believers and the widows and showed them that she was alive.
This became known all over Joppa, and many people believed in the Lord.
Peter stayed in Joppa for some time with a man named Simon, who made leather.
